bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Supply chain volatility in raw materials — Management explicitly flags fluctuations in the cost and availability of raw materials as a key risk to operations and performance, which can affect both input costs and product availability
- Regulatory compliance across domestic and international markets — The Company must ensure continuous compliance with evolving regulatory requirements in both domestic and international markets; the wider sector also faces regulatory uncertainty
- Pricing pressure and margin compression on digital and quick commerce platforms — Management states it operates in a highly competitive environment, particularly on digital and quick commerce platforms, where pricing pressures and margin challenges are significant — a structural risk given the Company's channel dependence
- Macroeconomic exposure — inflation, currency movements and global uncertainty — Management notes these broader factors may influence demand patterns and cost structures; currency exposure is relevant given an overseas subsidiary and international sourcing
- Intense competition from organised and unorganised players in a fragmented market — The home healthcare market remains highly fragmented with a large number of players across services, devices and digital health, adding to competitive intensity and the complexity of operating in the industry
- Low awareness and affordability constraints limiting adoption in India — Cited as a sector threat — low awareness and affordability constraints among large sections of the population, alongside uneven healthcare infrastructure across regions, may cap addressable demand
- Data privacy and limited digital literacy — Flagged as sector challenges that, together with dependence on skilled healthcare professionals, may impact scalability and profitability — relevant to the Company's digital ecosystem and health-data platform
- Need for continuous technological investment — The sector requires ongoing technology spending to stay competitive, adding to the complexity and capital intensity of operating in this evolving industry

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Positions itself as India's leading consumer healthcare platform spanning home healthcare, wellness and personal care, anchored on the Dr Trust, Dr Physio and Trumom brands rather than a single product category.
- Brand equity is presented as the core moat: Dr Trust holds 'Well Known Trademark' status, was ranked 'India's No.1 Home Healthcare & Wellness Brand' (2023), recognised by Pharmexcil as a household name, and uses Rohit Sharma as brand ambassador.
- Claims presence in all eight home-healthcare categories of the addressable Indian and neighbouring market, sized at ₹3,240 Cr in 2025 growing to ₹5,203 Cr by 2030E (9.9% CAGR).
- Omnichannel reach is a stated differentiator — online marketplaces, quick commerce, direct-to-consumer and offline trade including 20,000+ pharmacies.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [AI / digital] Dr Trust 360 now embeds AI-powered health insights — trend detection, baselines and personalised summaries — presented as the mechanism for scaling engagement off an installed device base.
- [Track record] Journey milestones: founded 2016 (digital-first Dr Trust), revenue crossed USD 10 Mn in 2019 on pure e-commerce, NSE/BSE listing in 2021, in-house manufacturing from 2022.
- [People] Certified 'Great Place to Work' (2024) and ranked among 'Most Innovative Companies of India' (2023).
- [Market data caveat] Industry sizing is sourced from Frost & Sullivan, other industry reports and Statista, with data extrapolated per company estimates.

business.body: Nureca operates in the Indian home-healthcare space, addressing demand for preventive healthcare, home diagnostics and wellness solutions. The Company reaches consumers through digital and quick commerce platforms alongside an expanding digital ecosystem, and describes its manufacturing capabilities as strengthened during the year. Its broader mission, as stated in the governance report, is to alleviate human suffering by delivering globally competitive, high-quality and affordable healthcare solutions.

outlook.body: Monetizing Dr Trust 360 app via premium subscriptions (diet plans, HbA1c estimates, family alerts); expanding into neighboring South Asian markets; launching wearable biosensors; licensing AI health algorithms to clinics.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Shift from a brand, product-development and distribution-led model to an integrated healthcare products company, adding in-house design and manufacturing so consumer insight, product development, manufacturing and market access work together
- Make manufacturing central to strategy — design and manufacture high-quality healthcare products in India, benchmarked against global standards and built around Indian consumer needs
- Develop the upcoming Sundran, Punjab facility as a modern healthcare manufacturing platform spanning medical devices, consumables, hygiene products and allied categories
- Keep India as the primary market for growth and the principal destination for manufacturing capacity; deepen penetration, expand distribution and serve more Indian households
- Build deeper and wider omni-channel reach across e-commerce, quick commerce, pharmacies, medical stores, modern retail and a growing distributor network
- Pursue exports selectively and progressively as a complement to — not a definition of — the domestic business, using a domestic manufacturing platform with robust quality systems and regulatory readiness
- Use technology and the digital/AI health-data platform in support of the products business rather than becoming a software company
- Phase capital investment in line with category opportunities and consumer demand, prioritising areas with strong consumer understanding, established distribution and a sustainable right to compete, while protecting the balance sheet
- Embed quality at every stage from design and material selection to production, testing, packaging and after-sales support; aim to be a dependable, efficient and competitive manufacturer rather than the lowest-cost one
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Nureca's principal expansion project is an upcoming manufacturing facility at Sundran, Punjab, described by the Chairman as one of the most important investments in the Company's history. It is being developed as a modern healthcare manufacturing platform spanning medical devices, consumables, hygiene products and allied categories, and is framed not merely as production capacity but as an integrated capability set covering product engineering, process control, automation, quality assurance, regulatory compliance, vendor development and continuous improvement. The stated rationale is greater control over quality, reliability, availability and accessibility, reduced dependence on long international supply chains, faster product-development and variant-launch cycles, improved availability and shorter replenishment cycles supporting the distribution push across e-commerce, quick commerce, pharmacies, medical stores, modern retail and the distributor network. India is stated to be the principal destination for this manufacturing capacity, with exports pursued selectively later. Management gives no commissioning date, capacity figure or capex amount; it says investments will be phased in line with category opportunities and consumer demand, approached with "both ambition and patience", and expects the expansion to create employment across production, engineering, quality, warehousing, procurement and supply-chain functions plus opportunities for local suppliers, packaging companies, logistics providers and ancillary businesses. The MD&A separately refers to the Company entering the current financial year building on strengthened manufacturing capabilities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural demand for preventive healthcare, home diagnostics and wellness solutions in India remains strong, supported by rising health awareness, increasing digital adoption and favourable demographic trends
- Global home healthcare market growth driven by demand for accessible, cost-effective care outside clinical settings, an ageing population and rising chronic-disease prevalence; Asia Pacific expected to be the fastest-growing region
- Rising healthcare costs globally accelerating the shift to more economical home-based care delivery models
- India's low per capita healthcare spending versus developed markets, plus rising incomes and government initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat and the National Health Mission, expanding the addressable opportunity
- Smartphone penetration, internet connectivity and post-COVID behaviour change sustaining consumer preference for home-based care and remote-monitoring devices
- Most in-demand categories cited as diagnostic monitoring devices, respiratory care equipment, mobility aids and other home-use medical devices supporting chronic disease management
- Margin/efficiency levers stated as strengthened manufacturing capabilities, quick commerce presence and an expanding digital ecosystem; manufacturing expected to improve availability, shorten replenishment cycles and speed response to demand
- Headwinds flagged: pricing pressure and margin challenges on digital and quick commerce platforms, supply chain volatility in raw materials, and macro factors including inflation and currency movements
- Highly fragmented market with intense competition from organised and unorganised players and a need for continuous technological investment
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Nureca is a debt-free, asset-light digital health leader in India, combining proprietary D2C e-commerce, in-house USFDA-certified manufacturing, and a data-driven AI app (Dr Trust 360) to dominate the home healthcare segment with high-margin, repeat-purchase products. Its virtuous flywheel of consumer insights → product innovation → online sales → brand loyalty creates an unreplicable moat.

The Company will move from building products for India to building them in India, taking greater control of design, manufacturing and delivery to reduce dependence on long international supply chains.
The Company will build deeper and wider reach across e-commerce, quick commerce, pharmacies, medical stores, modern retail and its distributor network.
Exports will be pursued carefully and selectively as a complement to the domestic business, enabled by a domestic manufacturing platform with robust quality systems and regulatory readiness.
Investments will be phased in line with category opportunities and consumer demand, with the Company committing to protect its balance sheet and allocate capital prudently as it scales.

Manufacturing investments will be phased in line with category opportunities and consumer demand, prioritising areas with strong consumer understanding, established distribution and a sustainable right to compete, while protecting the balance sheet.

As operations expand the Company expects to create employment across production, engineering, quality, warehousing, procurement and supply-chain functions, plus opportunities for local suppliers, packaging companies, logistics providers and ancillary businesses.

risks.note: The Company must ensure continuous compliance with evolving regulatory requirements in both domestic and international markets; the wider sector also faces regulatory uncertainty

risks.risk: Pricing pressure and margin compression on digital and quick commerce platforms
risks.note: Management states it operates in a highly competitive environment, particularly on digital and quick commerce platforms, where pricing pressures and margin challenges are significant — a structural risk given the Company's channel dependence

risks.risk: Macroeconomic exposure — inflation, currency movements and global uncertainty
risks.note: Management notes these broader factors may influence demand patterns and cost structures; currency exposure is relevant given an overseas subsidiary and international sourcing

risks.risk: Intense competition from organised and unorganised players in a fragmented market
risks.note: The home healthcare market remains highly fragmented with a large number of players across services, devices and digital health, adding to competitive intensity and the complexity of operating in the industry

risks.risk: Low awareness and affordability constraints limiting adoption in India
risks.note: Cited as a sector threat — low awareness and affordability constraints among large sections of the population, alongside uneven healthcare infrastructure across regions, may cap addressable demand

risks.risk: Data privacy and limited digital literacy
risks.note: Flagged as sector challenges that, together with dependence on skilled healthcare professionals, may impact scalability and profitability — relevant to the Company's digital ecosystem and health-data platform
The sector requires ongoing technology spending to stay competitive, adding to the complexity and capital intensity of operating in this evolving industry

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Nureca Limited is an Indian home-healthcare products company whose stated vision is "transforming lives through the patented products that support diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of illness through easy monitoring & analysis of health data".

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Nureca operates in the Indian home-healthcare space, addressing demand for preventive healthcare, home diagnostics and wellness solutions. The Company reaches consumers through digital and quick commerce platforms alongside an expanding digital ecosystem, and describes its manufacturing capabilities as strengthened during the year. Its broader mission, as stated in the governance report, is to alleviate human suffering by delivering globally competitive, high-quality and affordable healthcare solutions.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Nureca Technologies Private Limited — subsidiary: Indian subsidiary reported under Form AOC-1 Part A and listed as a subsidiary in the Ind AS related-party note; directors Mr. Saurabh Goyal, Mr. Aryan Goyal and Mr. Rajinder Sharma held directorships in group private companies during the year
- Nureca Healthcare Private Limited — subsidiary: Subsidiary till 29-09-2025; struck off from the Register of Companies on 03 December 2025 vide Notice No. STK-7/001058/2025. Mr. Aryan Goyal, Mr. Saurabh Goyal and Mr. Rajinder Sharma held directorships in it during FY25-26 until the striking off
- Nureca INC — subsidiary: Overseas subsidiary reported in USD in Form AOC-1 Part A (exchange rate stated as INR 94.65 per USD) and listed as a subsidiary in the Ind AS related-party note

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Monetizing Dr Trust 360 app via premium subscriptions (diet plans, HbA1c estimates, family alerts); expanding into neighboring South Asian markets; launching wearable biosensors; licensing AI health algorithms to clinics.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural demand for preventive healthcare, home diagnostics and wellness solutions in India remains strong, supported by rising health awareness, increasing digital adoption and favourable demographic trends
- Global home healthcare market growth driven by demand for accessible, cost-effective care outside clinical settings, an ageing population and rising chronic-disease prevalence; Asia Pacific expected to be the fastest-growing region
- Rising healthcare costs globally accelerating the shift to more economical home-based care delivery models
- India's low per capita healthcare spending versus developed markets, plus rising incomes and government initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat and the National Health Mission, expanding the addressable opportunity
- Smartphone penetration, internet connectivity and post-COVID behaviour change sustaining consumer preference for home-based care and remote-monitoring devices
- Most in-demand categories cited as diagnostic monitoring devices, respiratory care equipment, mobility aids and other home-use medical devices supporting chronic disease management
- Margin/efficiency levers stated as strengthened manufacturing capabilities, quick commerce presence and an expanding digital ecosystem; manufacturing expected to improve availability, shorten replenishment cycles and speed response to demand
- Headwinds flagged: pricing pressure and margin challenges on digital and quick commerce platforms, supply chain volatility in raw materials, and macro factors including inflation and currency movements
- Highly fragmented market with intense competition from organised and unorganised players and a need for continuous technological investment

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin ~73% (INR1536M revenue, INR126M EBITDA implies ~82% EBITDA margin on operations); low SG&A due to digital-first model; manufacturing cost control via in-house production and JIT inventory.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Reinvesting 100% of profits into R&D, digital marketing, and scaling manufacturing; no dividends or buybacks; zero debt implies conservative capital structure.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Nureca's principal expansion project is an upcoming manufacturing facility at Sundran, Punjab, described by the Chairman as one of the most important investments in the Company's history. It is being developed as a modern healthcare manufacturing platform spanning medical devices, consumables, hygiene products and allied categories, and is framed not merely as production capacity but as an integrated capability set covering product engineering, process control, automation, quality assurance, regulatory compliance, vendor development and continuous improvement. The stated rationale is greater control over quality, reliability, availability and accessibility, reduced dependence on long international supply chains, faster product-development and variant-launch cycles, improved availability and shorter replenishment cycles supporting the distribution push across e-commerce, quick commerce, pharmacies, medical stores, modern retail and the distributor network. India is stated to be the principal destination for this manufacturing capacity, with exports pursued selectively later. Management gives no commissioning date, capacity figure or capex amount; it says investments will be phased in line with category opportunities and consumer demand, approached with "both ambition and patience", and expects the expansion to create employment across production, engineering, quality, warehousing, procurement and supply-chain functions plus opportunities for local suppliers, packaging companies, logistics providers and ancillary businesses. The MD&A separately refers to the Company entering the current financial year building on strengthened manufacturing capabilities.

moat.body:
- Strengthened manufacturing capabilities, cited by management as a base for the current year's outlook
- Established presence in quick commerce channels
- Expanding digital ecosystem supporting customer engagement
- Continued product innovation and deeper channel penetration as stated levers
- Documented internal control framework with Standard Operating Procedures across functions, independently evaluated by Internal Auditors and reviewed by the Audit Committee
- Human-resource philosophy focused on capability building and retention; 154 employees on payroll as on 31 March 2026

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Shift from a brand, product-development and distribution-led model to an integrated healthcare products company, adding in-house design and manufacturing so consumer insight, product development, manufacturing and market access work together
- Make manufacturing central to strategy — design and manufacture high-quality healthcare products in India, benchmarked against global standards and built around Indian consumer needs
- Develop the upcoming Sundran, Punjab facility as a modern healthcare manufacturing platform spanning medical devices, consumables, hygiene products and allied categories
- Keep …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [AI / digital] Dr Trust 360 now embeds AI-powered health insights — trend detection, baselines and personalised summaries — presented as the mechanism for scaling engagement off an installed device base.
- [Track record] Journey milestones: founded 2016 (digital-first Dr Trust), revenue crossed USD 10 Mn in 2019 on pure e-commerce, NSE/BSE listing in 2021, in-house manufacturing from 2022.
- [People] Certified 'Great Place to Work' (2024) and ranked among 'Most Innovative Companies of India' (2023).
- [Market data caveat] Industry sizing is sourced from Frost & Sullivan, other industry reports and Statista, with data extrapolated per company estimates.
